sheet-20-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 20 is the lower, larger part of the sheet and covers a block field of Asbury Park lying between Main Street along the top of the part and Emory Street along its foot. Bond Street crosses the middle. The wide numbered avenues, 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Avenue, run up and down the page from left to right, and the sheet is turned with north towards the right. A heavy horizontal line above Main Street divides it from the upper part of the sheet, which shows a separate area of West Asbury Park, and the part is cut along that line. The ground is a residential district of small frame dwellings set on regular narrow lots, with stables and outbuildings behind them. Some lots hold larger houses, one lettered as the Church of the Holy Spirit, with its rectory beside it, and a few buildings are coloured pink for brick. The blocks are numbered 1 to 6 on this part. Water pipes with their sizes are marked along the streets. The outlines of neighbouring sheets are marked by their numbers at the edges: 22 at the left edge, 27 at the right, 25 below, and 35, 36 and 37 above. The scale bar at the foot reads 60 ft to one inch, and the part carries a compass rose beside the heavy line. A stamp reading Duplicate appears at the lower right corner.
notes: Printed scale 60 ft to one inch; the fitted 6.63 px/ft agrees.
The upper part of the sheet (West Asbury Park: Asbury Av., Prospect Av., Dunlevvy, W. Munroe Av.) is a separate part, not georeferenced; see unplaced.
Two parts: 1 main map, Main/Bond/Emory with 1st to 4th Av; 2 top strip above a heavy line, West Asbury Park (Asbury Av, Prospect Av, Dunlevvy, W. Munroe Av), north up on its own compass (not placed).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: top strip above the heavy line: West Asbury Park around Asbury Av, Prospect Av, Dunlevvy and W. Munroe Av, drawn north up (two junctions identified with low confidence gave an implausible rotation; needs step 6b: hand-picked junctions or parcel corners checked against sheet 40).

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 shows the heart of Asbury Park's old business district near Wesley Lake. Main Street runs along the top of the sheet and Bond Street and Emory Street cross it further down, with Mattison Avenue, Bangs Avenue and Summerfield Avenue running up and down the page as the cross streets. The sheet is turned with north towards the right. The Main Street frontage is dense commercial property in brick and frame, with Central Hall, the Baptist church and the City Hotel, while later rows along Bond Street hold stores, and a large department store of the Steinbach Co. with its power house nearby. The diagonal streets Cookman, Emory Avenue and Lake Avenue cut through the left half of the sheet, with stores, hotels and dwellings, many in pink brick, along Cookman. The lower right holds rows of frame houses. Wesley Lake with a foot bridge fills the lower left, with its shore drawn along Lake Avenue, and an outlined block of sheet 53 and a wedge of sheet 48 are shown there. Water pipes are lettered along the streets. Scale 60 ft to one inch, with compass rose at the lower centre.
notes: Cookman Avenue, Lake Avenue and the Wesley Lake shore streets were left out of the control because the modern streets there have been rebuilt.
Printed scale 60 ft to one inch; the fitted 6.64 px/ft agrees.
Main to Grand Av, Mattison/Bangs/Summerfield, Cookman and Lake Av along Wesley Lake; lake-end streets rebuilt and left out.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers four rows of blocks in central Asbury Park between Main Street, drawn along the top of the sheet, and Grand Avenue along the bottom, with Bond Street and Emory Street crossing the middle. The cross avenues running towards the ocean are Summerfield Avenue at the left edge, Munroe Avenue, Sewall Avenue, Asbury Avenue and 1st Avenue at the right edge. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the upper right, so the avenues run up and down the sheet and the ocean lies beyond the bottom edge. The Main Street frontage is commercial: rows of small stores with a tin shop, printing and sign painting shops, restaurants, barbers, a cobbler, a carriage shop, a second-hand furniture store, a paints and oils store, a wagon and harness shop and the Haviland and Co. livery. The rest of the sheet is mostly frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a bakery and Yost's Express on Munroe Avenue, the Columbia Water Co. office near Emory Street and a few stores. Institutions include the brick Asbury Park High School and its primary building between Bond Street and Summerfield Avenue, the Asbury Park Opera House near Grand Avenue, the First Congregational Church at Asbury Avenue and Emory Street, Trinity Episcopal Church, the brick Free Library and the House of the Good Shepherd, a boarding house in summer, between Asbury and 1st Avenues near Grand Avenue. Hotels and boarding houses such as the Helen Dale, the Melrose, the St. George and the Grand Avenue Hotel line the lower rows. Water pipes with their sizes are drawn in the streets, and outlines of the blocks on sheets 34, 35, 21, 20, 23 and 25 frame the edges.
notes: Munroe Avenue is Monroe Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.63 px/ft agrees with the scale bar.
Central Asbury Park: Main to Grand Av, Summerfield to 1st Av. Pilot. 60 ft scale, one part.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 shows the south edge of central Asbury Park where the town meets Wesley Lake. The sheet is drawn with north towards the top, unlike the sheets of the main commercial district, so Asbury, Sewall and Munroe Avenues run across the page and Grand Avenue and Heck run up and down it. Library Square, a park laid out with diagonal paths radiating from a central circle, fills the upper left. East of Heck and Bergh the top of the sheet is taken by the Metropolitan Hotel with its servants quarters and annex, with the Hollywood, the Matthew and the Hallehurst beside it. Below Asbury Avenue the blocks are mostly frame dwellings, boarding houses and small hotels, among them the Ten Broeck, the Belmont, the Bingham, the San Juan and the St. James, the Emerald, the Harlan, the Princeton and the Hotel Philadelphia and the Pierre Pont along a diagonal frontage. Institutions and trades include the Grand Av. Reformed Church, Browns Livery, M. Sexton's Livery, being built in iron clad, milk depots, a commercial house, and Menchens Johnstown Flood and Hereafter, an amusement building near Cookman. A large pavilion with offices and mineral water stands on a block east of Heck. The lower part of the sheet is crossed diagonally by Cookman, Heck and Lake, which follow the shore of Wesley Lake, drawn in blue with a foot bridge across it. A compass rose lies at the right. Water pipes with their sizes are marked in the streets, and neighbouring sheets 21, 22, 24, 25, 52 and 53 are indicated at the margins.
notes: Munroe Avenue is Monroe Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Heck is Heck Street.
Two diagonal streets on the east side of the sheet are lettered only 'Av.' with no legible name; they are left out of the street list.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.62 px/ft agrees. The compass shows north up the page, the rotation is about -15 degrees.
Streets along the ocean end of Wesley Lake (Cookman, Lake Avenue, Kingsley Avenue) were not used as control (rebuilt).
South edge at Wesley Lake: Asbury/Sewall/Monroe Av, Grand, Heck, Bergh, 1st Av, Library Square; drawn north up (rotation about -15).

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the ocean end of Wesley Lake, the boundary between Asbury Park on the right and Ocean Grove on the left, from Bergh Street at the top of the sheet to the beach and the Atlantic Ocean at the bottom. The sheet is turned on the page with north towards the right. On the Asbury Park side, between Asbury Avenue and 1st Avenue, stand the large frame West End Hotel, the Grammercy Hotel, Days ice cream parlor and the Ocean Pier Cottage above Kingsley Street, and the Coleman House, with its dining hall, bowling alley, billiard and dancing halls, below it. Between Lake Avenue, St. James Place and Cookman Avenue is a dense amusement block: the Palace merry-go-round, a ferris wheel, the Crystal Maze, an amusement parlor, a salt water swimming pool and hot baths, bowling alley and ice cream parlor, drug stores, restaurants and small hotels such as the Belle View, the Ocean Spray, the Raleigh, the Tremont House, the Astoria and the Newark Hotel; the Plaza Hotel faces Asbury Avenue near Kingsley. Below Ocean Avenue the boardwalk crosses the sheet with the Asbury Avenue Casino, booths and offices on the beach. Wesley Lake winds diagonally across the left half of the sheet. On the Ocean Grove side, along Lake Avenue and Ocean Avenue, rows of small tents and cottages fill the tenting grounds, with a swimming pool and, on the beach, the Ross pavilion and bath houses. A compass rose stands on the lake. Blocks of sheets 23, 25 and 26 are outlined at the edges.
notes: Kingsley is Kingsley Street east of Asbury Avenue and Kingsley Avenue west of it in OpenStreetMap; Bergh is Bergh Street.

The streets around the lake end (Cookman Avenue, St. James Place, Lake Avenue, Kingsley west of Asbury Avenue) have been rebuilt; their modern junctions sat 2 to 3 m off and pulled the scale 3 percent, so they were left out of control.
The Ocean Grove side has no control point; its placement rests on the Asbury Park side.

Wesley Lake ocean end: Asbury Park (Bergh to Ocean Av, Lake Av to 1st Av, amusement block, West End Hotel, Coleman House, Casino) and the Ocean Grove tenting grounds across the lake. One part; lake-end streets rebuilt, control from the grid side only.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers nine blocks of central Asbury Park lying between Emory Street, drawn near the top of the sheet, and Bergh Street near the bottom, with Grand Avenue and Heck Street crossing the middle. The numbered avenues, 1st to 4th, run up and down the page, which is turned so that north lies towards the right and the ocean beyond the bottom. The top row holds the First Presbyterian Church, a blue-coloured brick building with tower, among frame dwellings and boarding houses with names such as the McKinley Villa, the Bonaventure, the Oaks and the Alvord, and a central block labelled Educational Square. This block carries Whittier Hall, a shed and the octagonal Educational Hall with its stage, standing in an open square. The middle row has the First M.E. Church, drawn in pink with steam heat and electric light, and below it the large Y.W.C.A. of Phila'. with the Sea Rest and The Whelen wings and a platform. Beside it, between 2nd and 3rd Avenues, are the Minot Ho., open all year, and many frame dwellings and cottages. The bottom row is mostly frame hotels and boarding houses: The Chatsworth, The Garland, The Ashland, The New York, The St. John and The Pokeepsie. Printed widths of 100 ft for the avenues and Grand Avenue and 50 ft for Emory, Heck and Bergh Streets are given, with water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches in the streets, fire alarm boxes and hydrant marks. Outlines of sheets 20, 22, 23, 26, 27 and 29 frame the edges. A compass rose sits at top right and the scale bar of 60 ft to one inch at bottom left.
notes: Emory, Heck and Bergh are Emory Street, Heck Street and Bergh Street in OpenStreetMap.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.68 px/ft agrees.
Emory to Bergh, 1st to 4th Av, Educational Square.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows the ocean-front blocks of Asbury Park from Bergh Street, drawn near the top edge, past Kingsley Street across the middle, to Ocean Avenue, the Board Walk and the Atlantic Ocean at the bottom. The sheet is turned with north towards the right, so the avenues, 1st to 4th, run up and down the page, and the blocks are drawn narrowing slightly towards the ocean. The upper two rows are crowded with frame hotels and boarding houses, among them Tilton's Livery, the Hotel Ardsley, the Grand View, the Hotel Gladstone, the Willard, the Guy Mansion, the American Ho., the Lyndhurst, the Fenimore, the Manhattan, the Beachwood Inn, the Saint Charles with a row of stores below it, Nassau Hall, the Milton, the Addison, the Westminster, the Brighton, the Colonnade and many others. Between Kingsley Street and Ocean Avenue are the Surf Ho., the Imperial, the Grand Central, the Old Mill with its stage and dance halls, the Davenport Inn, Coopers Fairy Garden, the Albion, the Breakers, Johnstown Flood, the Asbury Park Roller Toboggan Chute, the Aberdeen, the Clifton, the Victoria, Edgemere Inn, Hotel Bristol and the Belvedere. South of Ocean Avenue stand the First Av., Third Av. and Fourth Av. groups of bath houses along the Board Walk, whose boards are shown in yellow hatching, with the shore and the Atlantic Ocean below. Printed widths are 100 ft for the avenues, 75 ft for Kingsley and 50 ft for Bergh. A compass rose, scale bar of 60 ft to one inch and Map Division stamps lie at the bottom right.
notes: Bergh and Kingsley are Bergh Street and Kingsley Street in OpenStreetMap.

The blocks are drawn narrowing towards the ocean; the avenue junctions on Kingsley Street disagree with modern positions by several metres, so only the Bergh Street row and 3rd Avenue are used as control.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.63 px/ft agrees.
Ocean front, Bergh to Ocean Av and the boardwalk, 1st to 4th Av; blocks drawn tapering towards the ocean (Kingsley row 345 m drawn against 391 m modern). Weak.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers the northern part of central Asbury Park around Sun Set Lake, between Main Street at the top and Grand Avenue at the bottom. The page is turned so that north lies towards the right. Down the left side, between 4th and 5th Avenues, are three rows of blocks of frame dwellings on narrow lots, numbered in the 500s to 700s, with a few named houses, among them the Rheinland, the Ideal View, the Wimbledon and the Ravenswood Inn. A large open block bounded by Main Street, Bond Street, 5th Avenue and Sunset Avenue is entirely blank, and below Bond Street the same block holds the irregular outline of Sun Set Lake, with several wooded islands, a bridge across its narrows, a footbridge to a promontory and a pavilion at the Grand Avenue end. Sunset Avenue runs down the right side, curving at the foot of the right-hand block, and beyond it, between Sunset and 6th Avenues, are blocks of lots that are mostly empty with a few frame dwellings. Printed street widths include 75 ft for Main Street, 50 ft for Bond Street and Emory Street, and 100 ft for the avenues and Grand Avenue. Dashed lines mark water pipes of 3, 4, 6 and 10 inches, with fire alarm boxes and hydrants at the corners. Outlines of sheets 20, 25, 28, 29, 36 and 39 are shown at the edges. A compass rose with its north needle stands on the lake and the scale bar of 60 ft to one inch is at bottom left.
notes: Main, Bond and Emory are Main Street, Bond Street and Emory Street in OpenStreetMap.
Sunset Avenue curves near Emory Street and Grand Avenue; those two junctions were left out of the control.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.62 px/ft agrees.
Main to Grand Av, 4th to 6th Av, Sun Set Lake north side.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 lies at the north edge of the built part of Asbury Park, between Main Street at the top and Grand Avenue at the bottom, and reaches east to the shore of Deal Lake. North lies towards the right. At left, between 6th and 7th Avenues, are four rows of blocks of frame dwellings along numbered lots, mostly 2 and 2 1/2 storeys, with outbuildings. Between 7th and 8th Avenues the blocks are laid out as lots, almost entirely vacant, with a few dwellings along 7th Avenue near the bottom; their east side is cut off diagonally by the shore of Deal Lake. A triangular block labelled Oak Bluff Av. lies against the lake, below which Emory Street ends at lake front lots with a few dwellings, one with a pink-coloured outbuilding. At the top right a wooden bridge 650 ft long and an electric railway bridge cross Deal Lake, and a 4 inch water pipe to Lock Arbour runs across the lake. Printed street widths are 75 ft for Main Street, 50 ft for Bond Street and Emory Street, and 100 ft for the avenues and Grand Avenue, with 8 inch and 6 inch water pipes drawn in the streets. Outlines of sheets 27, 39 and 31 appear at the edges, and a compass rose and the scale bar of 60 ft to one inch are drawn at the right and bottom.
notes: Oak Bluff Av. is printed with the abbreviation Av.; it is drawn along the Deal Lake shore.
Main, Bond and Emory are Main Street, Bond Street and Emory Street in OpenStreetMap.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.63 px/ft agrees.
6th to 8th Av, Main to Grand Av, to Deal Lake.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 centres on Sun Set Lake, the southern basin of the lake system, and is turned differently from its neighbours: north lies almost at the top of the page. Along the top, 6th Avenue passes north of two blocks of lots; the left one, with four frame dwellings, is bounded by Park Av., and the right one, between Park Av. and Webb, holds Holly Terrace, Rosedale Cottage, the Frederick and a row of cottages, with a drugstore at the corner. A second tier of blocks below Sunset Av. has the Cedars, Sunset Ay Ho., the Lakelyn and the Crescent. Sunset Av. runs diagonally across the sheet along the north shore of the lake, and Grand Av. crosses the lake on a bridge at the left. The lake itself fills the middle, spanned by a footbridge. At the bottom, between 5th Av. and 4th Av., two rows of hotels and boarding houses, the Hotel Touraine with its annex, the Leslie, the Hotel Stafford, the Clarendon, the Lafayette, the Park View and the Bermin, stand on either side of Heck and Bergh Streets. Printed widths are 100 ft for the avenues and 50 ft for Heck, Bergh and Webb. Water pipes of 3, 4 and 6 inches and fire alarm boxes are marked. Outlines of sheets 25, 26, 27, 30 and 31 frame the edges. The compass rose on the lake shows north slightly west of the top of the page, and the scale bar is at the bottom.
notes: Heck, Bergh and Webb are Heck Street, Bergh Street and Webb Street in OpenStreetMap.
This sheet is turned about 90 degrees from sheet 25 and its neighbours; north points nearly up (fitted rotation about -15 degrees).
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.66 px/ft agrees.
Sun Set Lake; drawn north up (rotation about -15).

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers the Asbury Park ocean front around Sunset Avenue, between 6th Avenue at the top of the sheet and 4th Avenue at its foot. The sheet is drawn with the Atlantic Ocean to the right and the map turned so that the streets run nearly straight up and down. Webb and Kingsley Streets run up and down at the left, with Ocean Avenue beside the Board Walk at the right. The two large open squares in the middle of the sheet, together named Atlantic Square, are drawn as dashed outlines crossed by diagonal walks, with the Asbury Park Auditorium standing on its own block in the upper centre. The left side holds the big seaside hotels, among them the Franklin, the Yorkshire, Hotel Monmouth, Hotel Waldorf, Sun Set Hall and Hotel Brunswick, with the Fifth Av Arcade built out on the beach at the lower right. The Board Walk is drawn as a long strip hatched in yellow with a pier. The Atlantic Ocean and its shore fill the right edge. Sheet numbers 29 and 26 are lettered at the left and bottom edges, and the sheet has a compass rose and a scale of 60 ft to one inch.
notes: Ocean Avenue junctions were not detected and Ocean Avenue is not used as control.
The sheet is rotated about 15 degrees from north (the fit gives about -15), which matches the compass rose.
Webb/Kingsley/Ocean Av, 4th to 6th Av, Atlantic Square; north up (about -15).

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 shows the north end of Asbury Park beside Deal Lake, between 6th Avenue at the foot of the sheet and Oak Bluff Avenue near the lake shore. Grand Avenue, Park Avenue and Webb Street run up and down the sheet from left to right, with 6th, 7th and 8th Avenue crossing them. The sheet is turned so that the lake lies at the top and the streets run nearly straight. Deal Lake crosses the top of the sheet in a pale blue band, and Oak Bluff Avenue follows the south shore. The area above 8th Avenue is open land in two large unbuilt tracts, numbered 1 and 2, with only a house and outbuildings on the second. Below 8th Avenue the blocks, numbered 3 to 6, are lined with frame dwellings and boarding houses with names lettered on them, such as the Le Roy, the Plymouth, the Northern and the Phoenix. A fire house, lettered Fire Ho No 4, stands in the lower middle. A compass rose sits near the centre and the scale bar, 60 ft to one inch, is printed at the foot. Sheet numbers 28, 29 and 32 are lettered at the edges.
notes: Oak Bluff Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and is not used as control.
Printed scale 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.67 px/ft.
Oak Bluff Av at Deal Lake, Grand/Park/Webb, 6th to 8th Av; north up (about -15).

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the northern end of the Asbury Park beach front between Deal Lake at the top of the sheet and 6th Avenue at its foot. Webb, Kingsley and Ocean Avenue run up and down the sheet from left to right, crossed by 6th, 7th and 8th Avenue. The Atlantic Ocean lies along the right edge, with the shore as a broad blue band and a compass rose beside it. Deal Lake crosses the top, and Oak Bluff Avenue runs along its shore above the numbered blocks. The northern blocks, numbered 1 to 3, are open land with a few small outbuildings. Below 8th Avenue the left half holds seaside hotels and boarding houses, among them Hotel Colonial and the Ocean View, the Knickerbocker, the Florida and Hotel Columbia, which stands at the lower left. The right half is open blocks numbered 3 and 6. At the right is the Board Walk, drawn as a hatched strip running out to the Seventh Av Group of Bath Hs, a rank of bath houses and a pavilion. Sheet numbers 31 and 30 are lettered at the lower left. Scale 60 ft to one inch.
notes: Ocean Avenue is not detected on this sheet; the placement rests on Webb and Kingsley.
Oak Bluff Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and is not used as control.
Ocean front at Deal Lake, Webb/Kingsley/Ocean Av, 6th to 8th Av; north up (about -15).

sheet-33-1.description: The main part of sheet 33 covers the west side of the railroad in Asbury Park, from Comstock Street at the top of the sheet to Main Street at the bottom, between the diagonal Prospect Avenue and Springwood Avenue on the left and Bangs Avenue on the right. Cookman Avenue, Mattison Avenue and Lake Avenue cross Langford Street and Railroad Alley. The sheet is turned on the page with north towards the right, so the avenues run up and down the sheet. The upper blocks hold frame dwellings and a few stores, with a small electrical works near Langford Street and a row of stores, a restaurant, a barber and pool rooms at the corner of Prospect and Springwood Avenues. The lower third is taken up by the tracks of the railroad, drawn as several parallel lines across the sheet, with the south bound and north bound platforms, a waiting shed and the passenger station near Bangs Avenue. Below the tracks, at Main Street and Springwood Avenue, is a dense brick business block with a harness and carriage shop, furniture storage, a produce store, harness and tobacco shops, an undertaker, a bakery, a jeweller, a drug store with upholstering above, a hardware store and a grocery, and behind them the Adams Express office, the Imperial Steam Laundry, the A. P. Steam Laundry, a feed and grain store and a lodge hall. Large empty blocks lie between Lake Avenue and Cookman Avenue along Railroad Alley. A separate inset in the top left corner, the East Jersey Coast Water Co. pumping station on Oxyonia Avenue, is drawn at another location and is not part of this part. A compass rose near Springwood Avenue gives north towards the right of the sheet.
notes: Lake Avenue west of the railroad has no counterpart under that name today and was not used for control.
Langford Street / Prospect Avenue was detected 10 m off the fit and rejected; Prospect Avenue appears realigned at its south end.

Two parts: 1 main map west of the railroad (Comstock to Main St, Prospect/Springwood to Bangs Av, station); 2 inset top left, East Jersey Coast Water Co. pumping station on Oxyonia Av by a Deal Lake branch, west of town (not placed).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: East Jersey Coast Water Co. pumping station on Oxyonia Avenue by a branch of Deal Lake (no street junction; Oxyonia Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap; needs hand-picked control (parcel corners or the shore of the Deal Lake branch near Asbury Avenue, west of the town)).

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers a district of West Asbury Park and the adjoining blocks of Asbury Park lying west of the New York and Long Branch Railroad, about as much as three blocks wide and four deep. The sheet is turned so that north lies to the right, and Bangs, Summerfield, Munroe, Sewall and Asbury Avenues run up the page while Comstock, Langford, Railroad Avenue and Main run across it. The upper two rows of blocks, between Comstock and Langford, are laid out in narrow lots that are only partly built up with frame dwellings, with a scattering of outbuildings. The middle row, between Langford and Railroad Avenue, holds more dwellings and a number of trades: the Star Bottling Works, W. A. N. Emmon's carriage factory with its wood working and painting shops, F. Kurrus's ice cream factory, the Reid Ice Cream Co., slate storage and several ice houses. Large parts of this row between Bangs and Summerfield and the lower lots near Railroad Avenue are blank, unbuilt ground. The railroad, marked N.Y. & L.B. R.R., crosses the sheet as a band of parallel tracks with a compass rose over it. Below the tracks, along Main, the blocks hold Weeden Havens & Weeden's carriage manufactory, Park Hall, sign painting and blacksmith shops, Hathaway Hall, the Asbury Park Beef Co., a machine shop, an automobile garage and Eagle Hall. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 12 inches are marked in the streets, and the adjoining sheets 20, 21, 22, 33, 35, 39 and 40 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Munroe Avenue is Monroe Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Comstock, Langford and Main are Comstock Street, Langford Street and Main Street.
Railroad Avenue is in OpenStreetMap but has no junction used here.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.67 px/ft agrees.
Comstock to Main across the railroad, Bangs to Asbury Av.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 shows the area of West Asbury Park and Asbury Park on both sides of the New York and Long Branch Railroad, between Asbury Avenue at the left and 3rd Avenue at the right. North lies to the right of the page, so Asbury, 1st, 2nd and 3rd Avenues run up the sheet and Comstock, Langford, Railroad Avenue and Main run across it. The top two rows of blocks, between Comstock and Langford, are laid out in long narrow lots with only a few dwellings; at the upper right is a large blank block with a compass rose. Between Langford and Railroad Avenue stand the industrial buildings: the Atlantic Coast Elec. Light Co. stations No. 1 and No. 2 with their dynamo rooms and a water tank, B. F. Parisen's machine shop, the City Storage Yard with green houses and a wagon yard, and, at the right, the large works of Buchanan and Smock Lumber Co. with lumber sheds, lumber piles, a shingle shed, a wood working machinery building and a sash and blind ware house, served by a branch track curving in from the railroad. The railroad itself crosses the sheet as a band of tracks lettered N.Y. & L.B.R.R. South of it, along Main, are E. Stout's coal and wood yard with a coal trestle, C. B. Smock boarding, Wilkinson Goods wholesale grocery, United Ice Co., J. W. Sutphin and Son Carriage Works, a marble works, the Bethel A.M.E. Church and the Consumers Coal and Supply Co. Water pipes are marked in the streets and sheets 22, 20, 34, 36 and 37 are named at the margins.
notes: Comstock, Langford and Main are Comstock Street, Langford Street and Main Street in OpenStreetMap.
The two rail crossings with 1st and Asbury Avenues were rejected as 6 to 9 m off the street fit; the track layout has changed.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.66 px/ft agrees.
Asbury to 3rd Av, Comstock to Main, railroad, lumber yard.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 lies in West Asbury Park north of Main, between 3rd Avenue at the left and Sun Set Avenue at the right, and it spans the New York and Long Branch Railroad. North lies to the right, so the avenues run up the page and Comstock, Langford, Maple, Railroad Avenue, Steiner Place and Main run across it. The upper left is mostly open ground: James A. Bradley's storage yard, enclosed by a high fence, with Equus Hall, a wagon and storage shed and small buildings, and next to it blocks of narrow lots with a few frame dwellings along the east side of 4th Avenue. The centre of the sheet is a large block, number 5, that is blank apart from a store house. At the right, between Langford and Railroad Avenue, are rows of frame dwellings with a few stables, a stove and a baking house. Along the edge of the sheet east of the railroad are the N. J. Coast Water Co. and the Asbury Park System, lettered along Sun Set Avenue. Below Railroad Avenue and the tracks, marked N.Y. & L.B.R.R., stand the North Asbury depot and a platform, the Consumers Coal and Supply Co., the Artificial Stone Mfg. Co., Coulter and Whans salt and paper ware house, and at the centre the M. W. and C. Pennypacker printing house with its press and composing rooms, an old hose house and a bell tower. A park with a compass rose lies in the lower right corner, and the scale bar is at the bottom.
notes: Sun Set Avenue is Sunset Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Comstock, Langford and Main are Comstock Street, Langford Street and Main Street.
5th Avenue / Langford Street has two modern nodes 62 m apart; one was excluded by coordinates.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.64 px/ft agrees.
3rd to Sun Set Av, Comstock to Main, railroad.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 shows the western part of West Asbury Park, between Asbury Avenue at the left and 3rd Avenue at the right, with Pine and Comstock crossing it. North lies to the right of the page. The upper left corner is cut by Central Av., a street running diagonally from lower left to upper right and bordered by a few frame dwellings and a block (number 10) whose lots follow its slant. Near the left edge stands the West Park M. E. Church with its tower, lighted by electricity and heated by a furnace. East of 1st Avenue the large blocks 2 and 5 are mostly empty, with a hen house and a few dwellings, and a street labelled New, drawn as a pair of dashed lines and marked proposed, crosses them. A compass rose lies at the upper centre. Blocks 3 and 4 along 2nd and 3rd Avenues are laid out in narrow lots with some dwellings and a garage, and the blocks south of Pine, numbers 6, 7 and 8, are almost entirely vacant lots with only a handful of dwellings. Water pipes of 4 and 8 inches are marked in Pine and the avenues, and the adjoining sheets 20, 35, 38 and 40 are numbered at the margins. The scale bar is at the lower left.
notes: Pine, Comstock are Pine Street and Comstock Street in OpenStreetMap. The street lettered New, marked Proposed, is drawn but not built then; it does not appear to survive.
Asbury Avenue / Pine Street has two modern nodes 59 m apart; one was excluded by coordinates.
Central Av. at upper left has no matching junction in the extract and was not used.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.66 px/ft agrees.
Asbury to 3rd Av, Pine to Comstock, Central Av diagonal.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 shows the north end of West Asbury Park where the built-up blocks run out to Deal Lake. North lies to the right of the page. Along the top the sheet is blank except for a compass rose, a stretch of Deal Lake drawn in blue at the upper right, and an ice house on its shore. Lake, a street running across the sheet, forms the upper limit of the platted blocks, and Whitesville Road comes in from the upper left as a diagonal street crossing it, with a second diagonal block edge on its east side. The platted blocks below Lake are mostly empty lots: a street lettered New and marked proposed is outlined in dashed lines across the blocks. Pine crosses the middle of the sheet and Comstock the bottom. The only buildings are scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings in narrow lots along 3rd, 4th and 5th Avenues, with a milk depot and an ice house at the left, a shed beside block 2, and, at the lower right between 5th and Sun Set Avenues, a primary school, an ice house and a milk depot with several dwellings. Water pipes of 3 and 8 inches and 6 inches are marked in the streets, and sheets 36, 37, 39 and 40 are named at the margins.
notes: Sun Set Avenue is Sunset Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Pine and Comstock are Pine Street and Comstock Street. Lake Street and Whitesville Road have no matching junction in the extract; the street lettered New (proposed) is drawn but not built then.
Only 4 bootstrap junctions were given; the detector found 8 points, 4 of them boundary points on streets cut by the sheet edge.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.64 px/ft agrees.
3rd to Sun Set Av, Pine to Comstock, Deal Lake and Lake St at top (no control there).

sheet-39-1.description: The main part of sheet 39 covers the northwest corner of Asbury Park near Deal Lake, between Sunset Avenue on the left and 7th Avenue on the right, from an enclosure at the top of the sheet down to Main Street along the bottom edge. The sheet is turned on the page with north towards the right, so the avenues run up and down the sheet. Most of the upper half is a large fenced ground enclosed by a high board fence, with a long frame grand stand, two stretches of bleachers along a curved track, a water tank and a privy; the curve of the fence and track is drawn crossing the end of 6th Avenue. A few frame dwellings stand on Sunset Avenue and 6th Avenue below the enclosure, and the Asbury Park sprinkling station, a small pump house with an electric motor and pump, stands east of 6th Avenue. Railroad Avenue and Steiner Place run along either side of the tracks of the New York and Long Branch Railroad, which cross the sheet above Main Street. Below the tracks the blocks between Steiner Place and Main Street are almost empty, with three dwellings near 6th and 7th Avenues. A branch of Deal Lake enters at the right edge, crossed by the railroad and by a water pipe to Loch Arbour. Water mains of the Asbury Park system and the East Jersey Coast system are drawn along Sunset Avenue and Maple Street at the left edge. The top right corner of the sheet holds a separate inset, outlined by a heavy line, which is not part of this part.
notes: The avenues here are drawn 100 ft wide with no parcel gap in the modern data; street_widths is set so the detector pairs their edges.
Railroad Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap under that name here.

Two parts: 1 main map, Sunset to 7th Av between a fenced grand stand ground and Main St, railroad and Deal Lake branch; 2 inset top right, west end of Sunset Av at Deal Lake with the A. S. Dayton Ice Cream Co. (anchored on Pine St / Sunset Av).

sheet-39-2.description: Inset in the top right corner of sheet 39, outlined by a heavy line: the west end of Sunset Avenue where it meets Deal Lake, near Pine Street. Sunset Avenue, drawn 100 ft wide, runs up the inset to the shore of the lake; a wooden bridge 320 ft long leads from its end across the water towards the north. On the lake side of the avenue stands the A. S. Dayton Ice Cream Co., a frame ice house with an upper floor and a small outbuilding on the shore. The large block on the other side of Sunset Avenue is left blank and numbered 38, since it is drawn on sheet 38. Pine Street is lettered at the bottom of the inset with an 8 inch water pipe and a 6 inch pipe turning into Sunset Avenue. The waters of Deal Lake fill the right side of the inset and wind along its upper edge. A north arrow points to the right. The inset is drawn at the same scale and orientation as the main sheet but shows ground several hundred metres to the west of it.
notes: Placed from one detected junction (Pine Street / Sunset Avenue) with the scale and rotation of the main part: low confidence.

Two parts: 1 main map, Sunset to 7th Av between a fenced grand stand ground and Main St, railroad and Deal Lake branch; 2 inset top right, west end of Sunset Av at Deal Lake with the A. S. Dayton Ice Cream Co. (anchored on Pine St / Sunset Av).

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 covers the north-western corner of the built-up part of West Asbury Park, in Neptune Township, where the street grid of Asbury Park gives way to diagonal roads. The sheet is turned with north towards the right, so Asbury Avenue runs up the right edge and Comstock Street along the bottom, and the ocean lies off the bottom of the page. The pattern is set by Prospect Avenue, which crosses from the lower left to the upper right, and by Church Street, which cuts diagonally from the upper left to Asbury Avenue, with Pine Street running in from Asbury Avenue to meet Munroe Avenue near the foot of the sheet. At their meeting near the top, Church, Prospect and West Munroe Avenue form a many-armed junction. The blocks are long and narrow and carry a thin scatter of frame dwellings, mostly two-storey with porches and outbuildings, on large lots with house numbers in the 1100s and 1200s. The only public building coloured is the West Park School, a brick building (pink) standing in its own lot between Washington Avenue and Munroe Avenue, and a small church is drawn near Pine Street. The Good Will Fire Co. No. 1 house, with one hose cart, one hook and ladder and a 1000 foot hose supply, stands on Munroe Avenue near Comstock Street. Four-inch, six-inch and ten-inch water pipes are marked in the streets. The sheet is lettered West Asbury Park, with neighbouring sheet numbers 20, 34, 37, 41 and 42 at its edges, and the scale note is 60 feet to one inch.
notes: Munroe Avenue is Monroe Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Church Street at Asbury Avenue and the Church / Monroe / Prospect junction were checked; the modern Asbury / Church / Pine node was left out because it lies between two drawn junctions.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.67 px/ft.
West Asbury Park: Church and Prospect diagonals, Summerfield to Asbury Av, Comstock; rotation about 74.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 shows a sparsely built district of West Asbury Park, in Neptune Township, south-west of the diagonal Prospect Avenue area. Unlike the sheets to its north-east, this one is drawn with north towards the top of the page, as its compass shows, so Summerfield Avenue runs along the top edge and Springwood Avenue along the bottom. Between them the cross streets are Bangs Avenue and Mattison Avenue, each 50 to 60 feet wide, and the avenues running down the sheet are 1st, 2nd and 3rd Avenue, with Naples Place, a narrow 30 foot street, and the slanting Ridge Avenue at the left. Most of the ground is laid out in large empty blocks numbered 1 to 9 with no buildings at all. Development is confined to the blocks along 1st and 2nd Avenues and to the Springwood Avenue frontage, where small frame dwellings and a few stores stand on narrow lots numbered in the 1200s and 1300s. A bakery and a grocery are drawn near 2nd Avenue and Springwood Avenue, and two Baptist churches, the Mt. Pisgah Baptist Church and the Mt. Moriah Baptist Church, stand on the Springwood Avenue frontage, together with a Eureka Fire Co. building with a bell tower. A hand laundry is marked on 2nd Avenue. Water pipes of four, six and eight inches run in Summerfield, Bangs and Springwood Avenues. The sheet carries the heading West Asbury Park and neighbouring sheet numbers 40, 42, 43 and 44, and a scale of 60 feet to one inch.
notes: North is towards the top of the page on this sheet (fitted rotation about -6 degrees), not to the right as on the sheets of Asbury Park proper.
Printed 1st, 2nd and 3rd Avenues are Atkins, Borden and Dewitt Avenues in OpenStreetMap; Springwood Avenue and Mattison Avenue keep their names.
Naples Place (Elizabeth Avenue in OpenStreetMap) and Ridge Avenue lie 5 to 8 m from their modern lines and were left out of the fit.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.65 px/ft.
West Asbury Park, Summerfield/Bangs/Mattison to Springwood, printed 1st to 3rd Av (Atkins, Borden, Dewitt); north up (about -6). Ridge Av and Naples Pl (Elizabeth Av) displaced, left out.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 shows the densest part of West Asbury Park, in Neptune Township, between Bangs Avenue at the top and Springwood Avenue at the bottom. The compass shows north towards the top of the page. Three long avenues slant down the sheet from upper left to lower right and then converge on Springwood Avenue: Union Avenue, Sylvan Avenue and Prospect Avenue, with 1st Avenue along the left edge and Comstock beside Bangs Avenue at the top. Mattison Avenue crosses the upper third. The upper blocks hold scattered frame dwellings and some larger sheds, and a sign painting shop and bicycle repair shop coloured green stands near Mattison Avenue. Below that the blocks between the avenues are filled with narrow lots of small two-storey frame dwellings, with stables, sheds and tenements, and a building marked as damaged by fire and the ruins of a building damaged by fire are drawn on the left. Institutions include the 2nd Baptist Church on 1st Avenue, St. Augustine's Chapel on Prospect Avenue, the Springwood Avenue School with its annex and the Lyric Hall near Springwood Avenue, a club house, and a number of stores, a bakery and a cafe on the Springwood Avenue frontage. Cookman Avenue, Mattison Avenue and Lake Avenue are shown as dashed streets running off to the right, towards sheet 33, and Langford Street runs along the lower right. Water pipes of four, six, eight and ten inches are marked. Neighbouring sheets 33, 40, 41, 44 and 45 are numbered at the edges, and the scale is 60 feet to one inch.
notes: North is towards the top of the page on this sheet (fitted rotation about -5 degrees).
Printed 1st Avenue is Atkins Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

Prospect Avenue and Langford Street were left out: their modern junctions sat 4 to 5 m from the drawn ones (Prospect Avenue appears to have been realigned). The part is placed from four points along the bottom and top rows, so the right-hand side has no direct control.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.62 px/ft.
West Asbury Park, Bangs to Springwood around Union and Sylvan Av, St. Augustins Chapel; north up (about -5). Weak: 4 points on two rows.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 covers the south-western part of West Asbury Park, in Neptune Township, from Springwood Avenue along the top of the sheet down to Embury Avenue near the bottom. The compass shows north towards the top of the page. The ground is divided by long slanting avenues, Myrtle Avenue and Ridge Avenue, which run down the sheet from upper left to lower right, Garfield Avenue and 2nd Avenue, which run straight down the right side, and a cross street lettered only Street, which crosses the middle between Myrtle and Ridge Avenues. Heck Avenue crosses the sheet below the middle, running slightly uphill to the right, and Embury Avenue, with its row of narrow lots, lies near the bottom, where Ridge Avenue continues south. Development is thin: scattered frame dwellings stand on long narrow lots along Myrtle and Ridge Avenues and in a row of small houses facing Embury Avenue, with a few larger blocks left open or marked only with block numbers 1 to 9. Named buildings include the Sprague Oriental, a boarding house, the Lynchburg Cottage and the Maryland Cottage, and several cottages on Embury Avenue. The blocks on 2nd Avenue at the right edge hold a row of small dwellings, while the large block between Garfield and 2nd Avenues is almost empty. Four-inch and eight-inch water pipes are marked at the edges. The heading West Asbury Park appears at the top, neighbouring sheets 41, 44 and 59 are numbered at the margins, and the scale is 60 feet to one inch.
notes: North is towards the top of the page on this sheet (fitted rotation about -5.6 degrees).
Printed 2nd Avenue and Garfield Avenue correspond to Borden Avenue and Dewitt Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
One cross street between Myrtle and Ridge Avenues is lettered only Street; its name is not printed on the sheet.
The Ridge Avenue / Springwood Avenue junction lies 7 m from its modern node and was left out (Ridge Avenue is drawn on a different alignment).
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.65 px/ft.
West Asbury Park south of Springwood, Myrtle and Ridge Av diagonals, Heck, Embury; north up (about -6).

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 shows the southern edge of the built-up area of West Asbury Park, in Neptune Township, where closely lotted blocks give way to large empty tracts crossed by a stream. The compass shows north towards the top of the page. Springwood Avenue runs along the top of the sheet and Adams, then Atlantic Avenue, cross it below, with 2nd Avenue, A Avenue, Atkins Avenue, Hetrick Avenue and Sylvan Avenue running down the sheet. Further south the broad Heck Avenue and Embury Avenue cross the sheet from left to right, rising slightly to the right, with Atkins Avenue continuing south across both. The densest frontage is on Springwood Avenue and Adams, where rows of small frame dwellings, stores and tenements stand close together, among them the A.M.E. Zion Church. The blocks on A Avenue hold the Metropolitan Hotel, the Church of God and the Saints of Christ, the White Head House, the Cottage Royal, a boarding house and a coloured chapel, and Snow Hill House stands on Atkins Avenue. Fields Villa and other houses occupy the blocks along Atlantic Avenue, where a strip of lots lies empty. A blue stream with branches runs from the left edge across the middle of the sheet, and Heck Avenue and Embury Avenue pass through unbuilt blocks numbered 6 to 9, with a wheelwright and paint shop of C. T. Hampton near the foot. Water pipes of four, six, eight and ten inches are marked. The heading West Asbury Park is at the top, neighbouring sheets 41, 42, 43, 45, 59 and 60 are numbered at the edges, and the scale is 60 feet to one inch.
notes: North is towards the top of the page on this sheet (fitted rotation about -5.5 degrees).
Printed 2nd Avenue is Borden Avenue in OpenStreetMap, A Avenue is Avenue A and Adams is Adams Street; the printed A. Av. was read as A Avenue.
Hetrick Avenue and the Atlantic Avenue drawn here have no modern counterpart (modern Atlantic Avenue lies to the north).
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.69 px/ft.
West Asbury Park, Springwood, Adams, Atlantic, Heck, Embury Av, Atkins; north up (about -6).

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 lies at the south-east corner of West Asbury Park, in Neptune Township, where the village meets the New York and Long Branch Railroad. The railroad runs as a bundle of parallel tracks down the right side of the sheet, and the blue line of a stream crosses the middle from the lower left to the right edge, passing under the railroad corridor. This sheet is turned a little more than the sheets to its west, so Springwood Avenue, Heck Avenue and Embury Avenue rise to the right while Sylvan Avenue and Prospect Avenue run down the page. A compass at the lower right shows north toward the top and a little to the left. The built-up part is the group of blocks at the upper left along Springwood Avenue, where a continuous row of stores faces the street: groceries, a bakery with its oven, hardware, restaurants and a block marked vacant. Behind them small dwellings stand along Wesley Place, Springwood Place and Sylvan Avenue, with Adams Street and Atlantic Avenue entering from the left edge. A large vacant block lies between Springwood Avenue and the stream. The lower half is almost empty, with Heck Avenue and Embury Avenue crossing long blocks numbered 7 and 9, a few dwellings, and the large Steinbach Co. warehouse beside Prospect Avenue. The heading West Asbury Park is at the top, neighbouring sheets 33, 42, 44, 48 and 60 are numbered at the edges, and the scale is 60 feet to one inch. Water pipes of four and ten inches are marked.
notes: The sheet is turned more than its neighbours: fitted rotation about -17 degrees against -5.5 on sheet 44.
Prospect Avenue south of Springwood Avenue is Memorial Drive in OpenStreetMap; the Memorial Drive / Springwood Avenue junction was left out (4 m off).
Wesley Place and Springwood Place have no modern counterpart; the lettering of Atlantic Avenue ends in Ay (read as Avenue).
The railroad is lettered N.Y. & L.B.R.R. (North Jersey Coast Line today); its Springwood Avenue crossing is one of the control points.
Printed scale: 60 ft to one inch; fitted 6.73 px/ft.
West Asbury Park, Springwood/Prospect (now Memorial Drive) at the railroad, Sylvan, Wesley Pl; rotation about -17.
